2019_141_101519regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting held October 15, 2019 at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. It pairs a consent agenda of September 2019 minutes and the August 2019 Treasurer's Report with a third-grade reading report and the Yeo & Yeo draft audit for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2019. August disbursements totaled $11,511,717.79, of which $9,592,895.76 was paid by check. The draft audit carried an unmodified opinion and reported total governmental fund balance of $69,101,705 at June 30, 2019, with a post-employment benefit obligation over $68M and net pension liability over $260M listed among future challenges.

**Meeting and logistics**
Troy School District Board of Education, Regular Meeting, October 15, 2019, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. District offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW), and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
TSD Mission Moment for George Freeman, computer tech at Hill and Morse Elementary Schools, who responded to a summer power outage at Boulan Park Middle School; introduced by Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning. A resolution names fifty-six Troy students as 2020 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists; more than 1,000,000 students from some 22,000 high schools entered and only 16,000 are selected, requiring scores in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT. Certificates were to be presented at an October 30th reception.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the September 3, 2019 Board Workshop; the September 17, 2019 Special Meeting, Closed Session and Regular Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for August 2019.

**Actions recorded in the September 17, 2019 minutes**
Resolution 19-079 approved a closed session on the purchase of real estate under the Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c). Resolutions 19-080 (consent agenda) and 19-081 (33 new hires) each passed Yes 6, No 0, Gottlieb absent. Resolution 19-082 authorized purchase from BTG Big Beaver LLC of 1522 E. Big Beaver Road, Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055, for not more than $4,000,000.00, to house TCCHS and Niles programs; Resolution 19-083 authorized bonds not to exceed $6,100,000 under Section 1351(2) of Act 451, PA 1976, available without a vote of the electors where bonded debt is under 5% of state equalized valuation. Both passed Yes 5, No 1 (Hammond), Gottlieb absent. Resolution 19-084 certified Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart, Karl Schmidt and Nicole Wilson to the MASB 2019 Delegate Assembly, November 8-11, 2019.

**2018-2019 audit (items 8.A and 8.B)**
Presented by David R. Youngstrom, CPA, Audit Partner, Yeo & Yeo, for the year ended June 30, 2019, watermarked DRAFT and previously shown at the October 1, 2019 Workshop. Unmodified opinion; no material weaknesses, significant deficiencies or material noncompliance. Total governmental fund balance $69,101,705 at June 30, 2019 against $67,009,508 at July 1, 2018; General Fund unassigned balance $24,623,618, or 16.02% of expenditures. Ten-year enrollment ran from 12,076 to 13,105.

2019_141_101519regmtg.verbose:
Agenda packet of the Troy School District Board of Education for the Regular Meeting of October 15, 2019, convening at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. Administration is at 4400 Livernois, telephone 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** The TSD Mission Moment honored George Freeman, computer tech at Hill and Morse Elementary Schools, who came in during an unexpected summer power outage at Boulan Park Middle School; Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, introduced him. A resolution signed "this fifteenth day of October, 2019" recognized fifty-six 2020 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, noting more than 1,000,000 entrants from some 22,000 high schools and only 16,000 semifinalists, qualification requiring the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT; certificates were to be presented at an October 30th reception.

**Minutes.** The September 3, 2019 Workshop ran 6:02 p.m. to 8:17 p.m. with Schmidt, Fleming, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson present alongside Superintendent Machesky and administrators Birmingham, Carrier, DiPilato, Haezebrouck, Griffor, Carson and West. At the September 17, 2019 Special Meeting, begun at 6:00 p.m. with Gottlieb absent, Resolution 19-079 (Philippart, supported by Hauff) took the Board into closed session under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), to discuss the purchase of real estate, running 6:05 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

The September 17, 2019 Regular Meeting ran 7:05 p.m. to 9:06 p.m. Recognitions included the Red Cross "District of Distinction Award" presented by Leonard Rezmierski and Kelly DeLong, citing Troy High senior Ian Watson; eleven 2019 spring All-State athletes; and the ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Comprehensive Annual Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2018, recognizing Rick West. Student representatives were Noah Germilhac (Troy College & Career High School), Pranay Gupta (International Academy - East), Noah Scudder (Athens High School) and Amanda Kovacs (Troy High School). MASB counsel Brad Banasik found that an email polling board members, which said "defer to majority of board members," violated the Open Meetings Act; Mrs. Hammond's motion to remove items 8A and 8B died for want of support.

Resolution 19-080 approved the August 20, 2019 minutes and the July 2019 Treasurer's Report (Yes 6, No 0, Gottlieb absent). Resolution 19-081 approved 33 new hires (Yes 6, No 0), Jordan Harris, Assistant Superintendent, Employee Services, citing retirements, resignations, leaves, FTE status and enrollment. Resolution 19-082 authorized purchase from BTG Big Beaver LLC of 1522 E. Big Beaver Road, City of Troy, County of Oakland, Sidwell No. 20-26-200-055, at a price not to exceed Four Million and 00/100 Dollars ($4,000,000.00). The "ITT Building" was discussed as the future home of TCCHS and Niles programs; Mrs. Hammond objected that TCCHS runs at a deficit, and Mr. Schmidt said waiting for the next bond proposal would delay opening until 2026. Vote: Yes 5, No 1 (Hammond), Gottlieb absent. Resolution 19-083 authorized bonds not to exceed Six Million One Hundred Thousand Dollars ($6,100,000) under Section 1351(2) of Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, which permits borrowing without a vote of the school electors where bonded indebtedness is less than 5% of state equalized valuation, with notice posted under Section 308 of Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001; Vote: Yes 5, No 1 (Hammond). Resolution 19-084 certified Gary Hauff, Nancy Philippart, Karl Schmidt and Nicole Wilson to the MASB 2019 Delegate Assembly, November 8-11, 2019. Non-agenda speakers were Lisa Efros (7053 Cathedral, Bloomfield Hills), Jennifer Cook (3856 Normanwood Drive, Orchard Lake), Kasia Lynch (55 Pond Street, Ortonville), Dr. Anne Hooghart (44610 Ludlou, Novi) and Chad Hiser (218 Cherry Drive, Troy). Dr. Machesky stated that had legislators kept funding up with inflation since the 2005/06 school year, the District would be operating with $33 million more annually.

**Third Grade Reading and Gap Analysis (item 7.A).** Reported October 1, 2019 by Kristine Griffor, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction; no action required. Slides covered the OneTROY mission statement, MTSS structure, subgroup monitoring for ED, EL and SE across 2017, 2018 and 2019, elementary grade-level meetings held three times per year to build Individual Reading Improvement Plans (IRIP), and new daily K-1 phonics instruction researched by the Teachers College Reading and Writing Project.

**2018-2019 Audit (items 8.A and 8.B).** David R. Youngstrom, CPA, Audit Partner at Yeo & Yeo, presented the DRAFT report for June 30, 2019, a draft having been shown at the October 1, 2019 Workshop; the financial statements received an unmodified opinion. Governmental funds balance sheet: cash and investments of 25,963,734 (General), 13,695,431 (2016 Capital Projects), 4,934,469 (Early Childhood Learning Center), 27,059,685 (2019 Capital Projects) and 6,149,493 (nonmajor), totaling 77,802,812; total assets 98,765,368; accrued payroll related liabilities 16,438,215; total liabilities 29,663,663; restricted for capital projects 39,282,689, debt service 2,392,659 and food service 174,644; committed 841,222; assigned capital projects 967,974; unassigned 24,623,618; total fund balance 25,406,493 / 11,238,933 / 832,206 / 26,940,023 / 4,684,050, totaling 69,101,705. Revenues and other sources totaled 213,439,845 against expenditures and other uses of 211,347,648, a change in fund balance of 2,092,197, with fund balance of 67,009,508 at July 1, 2018. General Fund revenue: Local $39,498,087 (26%), State $102,636,252 (67%), Federal $3,845,504 (2%), Interdistrict $7,817,110 (5%), Other $43,902. General Fund expenditures for the year ended June 30, 2018 by object: Salaries $76,254,967 (50%), Employee Benefits $48,985,232 (32%), Purchased Services $19,391,052 (13%), Supplies and Materials $6,630,625 (4%), Capital Outlay $381,395, Other $2,033,563 (1%). For the year ended June 30, 2019 by function: Instruction $105,006,674 (68%), Supporting Services $48,551,469 (32%), Other $118,691. Instructional expenditure comparison showed Troy at 68%, 69%, 69%, 69% and 68% across 2014-15 through 2018-19 against an average of all Oakland County schools of 62% in 2017-18. Per-pupil labels printed were $11,739, $11,094, $11,145, $10,812, $11,353, $11,596, $10,924, $11,028, $11,516 and $11,727. Ten-year enrollment ran 12,076; 12,032; 12,312; 12,438; 12,591; 12,563; 12,717; 12,881; 13,089; 13,105. General Fund unassigned balance history: $21,038,513 (15.76%), $20,231,419 (14.74%), $23,716,299, $24,786,571 (16.52%) and $24,623,618 (16.02%). No material weaknesses, significant deficiencies or material noncompliance were identified, with unmodified opinions on the Special Education Cluster and Title II, Part A - Supporting Effective Instruction major programs. Management comments cited prior-year federal procedures in progress, corrected athletic receipt procedures, and current-year federal policies and procedures. Future challenges listed rising fringe benefit costs, retirement rate increase, post employment benefit obligation over $68M, and net pension liability over $260M.

**Other items.** Item 10.A seeks approval, required by Board Policy 1000.01, Organization and Functioning of the Board; Reimbursement of Expenses, for Board Secretary Gary Hauff, Trustee Steve Gottlieb and Trustee Nicole Wilson to attend the National School Boards Association Advocacy Institute Conference in Washington, D.C., February 1-4, 2020. Item 10.B ratifies an International Academy governance amendment adopted by the Joint Steering Committee on October 2, 2019, approving "Alternative Number 1" attached to September 25, 2019 correspondence from Board Presidents Schmidt and Wiseman: the Consortium would be governed by a five-member body of the representatives of its three Fiscal Agents plus two at-large members elected by majority vote of all Participating Districts, at-large members serving two-year terms. Certification is signed by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education of Troy School District, Oakland County, Michigan, under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended.
